questions.question: An electrical fire should only be extinguished by:

options.text: the use of foam-type fire extinguishers
the use of carbon tetrachloride fire extinguishers
the use of soda-acid-type fire extinguishers

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Soda-acid and foam-type extinguishers are solutions prepared in water, which conducts electricity. As a result, it might generate an electric shock leading to short-circuiting and starting another fire. Hence, they are not used to extinguish electrical fires.

The use of carbon tetrachloride fire extinguisher is used to extinguish the fire.

questions.question: Halon/CTC type fire extinguisher is used to extinguish __________.
questions.solution:
A fire extinguisher, flame extinguisher or simply extinguisher is an active fire protection device used to extinguish or control small fires, often in an emergency situation.

Many types of fire extinguishers are available with different extinguishing 'agents' to deal with different classes of fires. 

Water-filled extinguishers 

There are two methods of operation.

 
• Gas cartridge type
 
• Stored pressure type

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d92271fe2583ac0a8ad7300024f1a962d711ecd61466797a1769f2857071557.png] 

Foam extinguishers:

These may be of stored pressure or gas cartridge types.

Foam extinguishers are most suitable for:

 
• flammable liquid fires
 
• running liquid fires

Must not be used where electrical equipment is involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6d0495118cc80cddc6d6350dac33789dc781751cd8f2682a12041cc07f9d4f0.png] 

Dry powder extinguishers:

 
• Extinguishers fitted with dry powder may be of the gas cartridge or stored pressure type.
 
• The main distinguishing feature is the fork-shaped nozzle.
 
• Powders have been developed to deal with class D fires. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e49d0e5a1b2b86cf263d9814e7c18669588657b4c7ec369e7368ca63548ecc48.png] 

Carbon dioxide (CO2):

 
• This type is easily distinguished by the distinctively shaped discharge horn.
 
• Suitable for class B fires
 
• Best suited where contamination by deposits must be avoided.
 
• Not generally effective in the open air.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/251827234bbbe33fa36f88f2da299618f6a81364aea1d7a19f916e9814ddbc35.png] 

Halon extinguishers:

 
• These extinguishers may be filled with carbon tetrachloride (CTC) and bromochlorodifluoro methene (BCF).
 
• They may be of either gas cartridge or stored pressure type.
 
• They are more effective in extinguishing small fires involving pouring liquids.
 
• These extinguishers are particularly suitable and safe to use on electrical equipment as the chemicals are electrically non-conductive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cfaddfb3961883489707a5e8e383199bbd34459af85f7190d2b659410905bd4.png]

questions.question: Which of the following IE rules stands for "Danger Notices"?
questions.solution:
**IE Rule 35 describes the IE rules that stand for "Danger Notices".**

This rule states that " Every medium, high and extra-high voltage installation shall affix permanently in a conspicu­ous position a danger notice in Hindi or English and the local language of the district, with a sign of skull and bones". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91770f10436cf9b7dd85ea2ab54163419a399d5d580ea4447a4c75bb61020f90.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• IE Rule 45 - Precautions to be adopted by consumers, electrical contractors, electrical workmen, and suppliers while electrical installation.
 
• IE Rule 43 - Fire buckets filled with clean dry sand and ready for immediate use for extinguishing fires shall be conspicuously marked and kept in all generating stations, enclosed sub-stations, and switch stations in a convenient situation.
 
• IE Rule 42 - Where A.C. and D.C. circuits are installed on the same support they shall be so arranged and protected that they shall not come into contact with each other when live.

questions.question:
Given below are two tools, namely:

(a) Voltage Operated Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker or 'ELCB'.

(b) Current Operated ELCB, formally called Residual Current Circuit Breaker or 'RCCB'.

Which of the following options is incorrect for these devices?

options.text: One terminal of the ELCB relay is connected to the metal part of the equipment to be protected and the other to the ground wire.
Standard RCCBs work fine for standard waveforms, but they are not guaranteed to work on non-standard waveforms such as pulsed DC.
The RCCB is connected with both phase and neutral wire, but not with grounded wire, and is tripped when the currents in both are not equal.
ELCBs are very sensitive to fault conditions hence sometimes troublesome trips.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4): (ELCBs are very sensitive to fault conditions hence sometimes troublesome trips.)

__**Concept:**__

 
• **An Earth-leakage circuit breaker **(ELCB) is a safety device used in electrical installations with high Earth impedance to prevent shock.
 
• It detects small stray voltages on the metal enclosures of electrical equipment. ELCB or Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers are mainly used to protect a device/equipment from leakage of current.
 
• The leakage current is caused due to partial touching of the live conductor with a metallic body of the equipment.
 
• The working principle of voltage ELCB is quite simple. One terminal of the relay coil is connected to the metal body of the equipment to be protected against earth leakage and another terminal is connected to the earth directly.
 
• If either of the earth wires becomes disconnected from the ELCB, it will **no longer trip **or the installation will often no longer be properly earthed. Some ELCBs do not respond to rectified fault currents. **so option 4 is wrong.**
 
• **A Residual Current Circuit Breaker (RCCB)** is an important safety measure when it comes to the protection of electrical circuits. The RCCB is connected with both phase and neutral wire, but not with grounded wire, and is tripped when the currents in both are not equal. Standard RCCBs work fine for standard waveforms, but they are not guaranteed to work on non-standard waveforms such as pulsed DC.

questions.question: What is low cost protection for an electrical system?
questions.solution:
**Rewirable fuse is a low-cost protection for an electrical system.**

__**Fuse wire**__

__
 
• In electronics and electrical engineering, a fuse is an electrical safety device that operates to provide overcurrent protection of an electrical circuit.
 
• Its essential component is a metal wire or strip that melts when too much current flows through it, thereby stopping or interrupting the current. 
 
• ​It is a one-time-use device; once a fuse has operated in an open circuit, it is of no use and must be replaced or rewired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A circuit breaker is an electrical safety device designed to protect an electrical circuit from damage caused by an overcurrent or short circuit. Its basic function is to interrupt current flow to protect equipment and to prevent the risk of fire.
 
• An isolator is a type of disconnecting switch which is used in an electrical circuit to ensure that the circuit is totally isolated from the supply mains

questions.question: Which of the following is used to provide mechanical protection to cables ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer Is option 3):(Armoured wire)

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• Steel wire armor provides mechanical protection to the cable. It means the** armored cable can withstand higher stresses**. It is also suitable for underground installations.
 
• The shield is normally grounded, and can sometimes be used as a protective circuit conductor (”ground wire”) for cable-supplied equipment.
 
• Armored cables are used in applications where cables will be exposed to mechanical or environmental damage under normal operating conditions. These applications include power circuits in industrial plants, commercial buildings, processing plants, and central and substation utility applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Construction Of Underground Power Cables:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a2140495108288a3cb105ae7dcf2dec983759cbd21d620f90f7bdb6c7c82d638.png] 

Conductor:

 
• Usually, 1 or 3 conductors (depending on the application) are used.
 
• These conductors are stranded to reduce skin effect, and proximity effect, and to keep it flexible.
 
• Conductors are made from electrolytic grade pure copper or aluminum.

Conductor screen:

 
• It is a semi-conducting tape or an extruded layer of a semi-conductive compound.
 
• Conductor screening is generally used in medium-voltage and high-voltage cables to maintain uniform electric fields and minimize electrostatic stresses.

Insulation:

 
• It is provided to withstand electrostatic stress.
 
• Various types (and thicknesses) of insulators like VIR (Vulcanized India Rubber), Impregnated paper, PVC (polyvinyl chloride), and XLPE (Cross-linked polyethylene) are utilized depending upon the applied voltage.

Insulation screen:

 
• A layer of semi-conductive material is generally used in medium-voltage and high voltage lines.
 
• It serves a similar purpose as that of the conductor screen.

Metallic Sheath:

 
• It provides protection to the cable from moisture and other chemicals (acids or alkalies) present in the environment or soil.
 
• It’s usually made up of Aluminium or Lead.
 
• It also provides a path for fault and leakage currents as the sheath is earthed at one cable end.

Bedding:

 
• It is a low-grade insulator like Jute or Hessian which protects the metallic sheath from corrosion and from mechanical injury due to armoring.

Serving:

 
• Another layer of low-grade insulators like Jute or Hessian or a thermoplastic compound like PVC is again provided to protect the steel from atmospheric contaminants and agents.

questions.question: What should be applied on tools to avoid rust in rainy season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1):(Grease)

__**Concept:**__

 
• One way to prevent rust on ferrous metals is to cover the surface with a coating such as paint, oil or grease, to prevent moisture and air from making direct contact with the metal
 
• When metal is coated in grease it forms a protective barrier that stops any external elements from seeping through. This includes water. As H2O is unable to penetrate the metal, the rusting process doesn't start. As well as tangible water, oil also repels the water that's present in oxygen.
 
• **Grease should be applied on tools to avoid rust in rainy season**

questions.question: Which of the following tools is not found in the tool-kit of an electrician?
questions.solution:
The Vice tool is not found in the toolkit of an electrician.

It is a mechanical tool.

 
• It is a device consisting of two parallel jaws for holding a workpiece; one of the jaws is fixed and the other is movable by a screw, a lever, or a cam.
 
• It is used for holding a workpiece during hand operations, such as filing, hammering, or sawing, and is permanently bolted to a bench.
